ai.title: calculate-monthly-usage script shows user details
ai.summary: The `calculate-monthly-usage` script now joins `schema.user` to fetch `name`, `email`, and `handle`. The top 10 users list displays these details instead of just the user ID. Also fixes `getCurrentMonthLocal` to use 0-based month indexing correctly.

eli5.text: The monthly usage report now shows the names, emails, and handles of the top 10 users instead of just their account IDs. If you run the report internally, you'll see friendlier labels like "John Doe (user-123)" along with emails like john@example.com and handles like @johndoe. A small date bug was also fixed so the report now uses the correct month when run at the start of a new month.

ai.title: Suppress websocket console logs unless verbose
ai.summary: WebSocket client error and warning logs in `common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts` now require `VERBOSE_LOGGING` to be enabled. This prevents console noise from reconnection failures, stale transaction IDs, and unknown message types during normal operation. The change applies to the shared core websocket layer used by all surfaces.

eli5.text: If you use an app or service powered by this platform, you will see far fewer error messages in your browser's developer console when the real-time connection drops or receives an odd response. The system still notices and recovers from these moments, but it now stays quiet about reconnection failures, stale transaction IDs, and unrecognized message types unless a special verbose logging mode is turned on. This affects all surfaces that rely on the shared real-time communication layer.

ai.title: SDK custom-tool import path fix
ai.summary: custom-tool.ts imports ToolResultOutput from '../../common/src/types/messages/content-part' instead of '@codebuff/common/types/messages/content-part'. Fixes SDK import resolution. Scope limited to sdk/src/custom-tool.ts.

eli5.text: The SDK had a broken link for looking up a piece of its own shared definitions. Developers building add-ons for the assistant can now import the tool-result type again, the path now points at the actual shared folder instead of a missing shortcut alias, so the type resolves correctly and custom tools stop failing to load in this part of the SDK.

If you use Codebuff's developer toolkit in your own projects, you're now running version 0.1.21. This is a small behind-the-scenes update that bumps the toolkit's version number, helping developers keep track of which version they're using and ensuring compatibility with the latest Codebuff services. There's nothing visible you'd notice if you looked, but the updated version number helps you stay in sync with other recent changes to how the toolkit connects and works.

ai.title: Rename constants to old-constants in backend and agents
ai.summary: Internal refactor renames `@codebuff/common/constants` imports to `@codebuff/common/old-constants` across backend services and agent factories. This isolates legacy constant definitions from the active `constants` module, likely preparing for a split between old and new model/config definitions. Scope covers `.agents/factory/*`, `backend/src/admin/*`, and core API handlers like `usage.ts` and `org.ts`. No user-facing behavior changes; purely structural import path updates.

eli5.text: The team reorganized how the assistant definitions store their settings and model references, moving the old configuration values into a separate labeled folder behind the scenes. If you looked at the code, you'd see references that used to point to the main settings file now point to a folder marked for legacy configs, but nothing about how the assistant behaves has changed. This is purely organizational cleanup with no visible effect for anyone using the system today.

ai.title: model-utils.ts import switched to old-constants
ai.summary: model-utils.ts now imports models from old-constants instead of constants. This aligns the dynamic require call with the type import, ensuring the explicitly defined models set is populated from the correct source. Scope is limited to common/src/util/model-utils.ts. The change fixes a mismatch where the type was sourced from old-constants but the runtime value was pulled from constants.

eli5.text: The list of available models the assistant can use is now read from a single, consistent source, so there is no longer a mismatch where the model names were being pulled from two different places. You may notice that the set of models offered stays steady and matches what was expected, instead of occasionally showing an outdated mix. The change is already live and affects anyone relying on the model list.

ai.title: Agent types import Message from @codebuff/sdk
ai.summary: Agent definition and tool types now import `Message` from `@codebuff/sdk` instead of local files. Local type definitions (`codebuff-message.ts`, `content-part.ts`, etc.) are removed from `.agents/types` and the `initial-agents-dir` template. This deduplicates message schema definitions, relying on the SDK as the single source of truth for agent types. The change affects both the internal agent configuration and the scaffolding generated by `init-agents`.

eli5.text: The assistant's message definitions, which previously lived as local files in both the main project and the starter template, are now pulled from a shared library called the SDK. This removes about 430 lines of duplicate type definitions across 15 files, leaving a single, authoritative copy maintained by the SDK. If you were to look at the project today, you would see those local message-related files gone and imports pointing to the SDK instead, meaning any future changes to how messages are structured will come from that shared library rather than being edited locally. This is live now and affects anyone using the starter template to build new agents, since they will inherit the SDK-managed types instead of local copies.

ai.title: Remove legacy evals infrastructure
ai.summary: Deleted evals directory containing e2e-cat-app-script.ts, swe-bench-eval.ts, swe-bench-ids.ts, and test-repos.json. Removed SWE-Bench integration scripts, instance ID mappings, and repo configuration files. Internal cleanup of obsolete evaluation tooling.

eli5.text: If you looked in the project's folders today, you'd find that the internal team removed several files they used to run automated tests, which were scripts and lists for checking the software against outside programming problems. These tests helped them measure how well their code fixing tool worked, but they are no longer using that system and have cleared it away completely.

ai.title: Remove pluralize import from code-map parse.ts
ai.summary: The `pluralize` utility import was removed from `packages/code-map/src/parse.ts`. The debug log statement in `getFileTokenScores` was updated to use a template literal directly instead of calling `pluralize`. This change simplifies the dependency graph for the code-map package.

eli5.text: The software removed a helper that was used to turn words into their plural forms (like adding an 's'). It only affected a behind-the-scenes message that developers see when they turn on extra logging to watch what the program is doing, so it does not change anything you see. The message now just says e.g. 'Parsed 5 files' instead of using the helper to decide whether to write 'file' or 'files'. This is internal housekeeping that trims an unnecessary tool for people who build and tune this software.

ai.title: Add evals README documenting commit reimplementation framework
ai.summary: New evals/README.md details the Git Commit Reimplementation Evaluation system. It describes the multi-turn interactive process where a prompting agent guides coding agents to reconstruct real git commits, followed by AI judging across completion, efficiency, code quality, and overall dimensions. The doc covers architecture components (orchestrators, runners for Codebuff/Claude, judging via Gemini 2.5 Pro), usage commands, data formats, and directory structure.

eli5.text: The team added a new guide explaining how they test the coding assistant's skills. Instead of just running simple quizzes, they now measure how well the assistant can rebuild actual software changes from real open-source projects, with an AI judge checking the work across correctness, efficiency, and code style. This guide lives only inside the company's internal testing system and won't change what you see in the product today.

ai.title: SDK README examples wrap code in async main function
ai.summary: Top-level await usage in `sdk/README.md` examples replaced with `async function main()` wrapper. Ensures snippets are valid in CommonJS or strict module contexts without relying on top-level await support. Affects basic and advanced usage documentation.

eli5.text: If you follow the setup instructions in the SDK guide to connect your own account, you will now see the example programs written as a single block of instructions that your computer runs from top to bottom, rather than as a list of commands that run one-by-one on their own. This means the code you copy will work whether your system runs the latest style of JavaScript or an older one, so you will not hit a confusing stop if your software does not understand commands written outside of a step-by-step instruction list.

ai.title: Agents types revert to local codebuff-message
ai.summary: Agent definition and tool types now import `Message` from local `./codebuff-message` instead of `@codebuff/sdk`. New Zod v4 schemas for messages, content parts, data content, JSON values, and provider metadata added to `.agents/types` and `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types`. This decouples agent templates from the external SDK dependency. `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/init-agents.ts` updated to reflect these local type imports.

eli5.text: If you set up new agent templates from scratch, those agents now carry their own copy of the message handling code instead of pulling it from the shared toolkit package. The system added local blueprints defining how messages, images, files, and tool calls are structured, and rewired the template generator to use these local copies. Nothing changes for agents already running, and the toolkit package remains available for other parts of the platform; the shift only affects freshly created agent templates going forward.

ai.title: SDK 0.1.22
ai.summary: Version bump to 0.1.22 in `sdk/package.json`. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The software development kit that lets other tools connect to and build on top of the assistant quietly moved from one patch version to the next with no new features or fixes, just an internal version-number bump. Nothing you use changes, and you won't see any difference in behavior, but if you were tracking which version you're on, it now reads a hair higher.

ai.title: CodeDemo horizontal scroll fix
ai.summary: Aligns padding and separator margins in `code-demo.tsx` to stabilize layout. Moves `px-4` from header/content to container, removing redundant horizontal margins from `Separator`. Fixes horizontal scrollbar issues across breakpoints in docs.

eli5.text: When you view code examples in the documentation, you may have noticed a horizontal scroll bar appearing that made the page wider than necessary. The layout instructions for the code display area have been adjusted so the spacing around the code and its header now line up neatly, which stops the page from stretching sideways and triggering that extra scroll bar. This only affects the documentation pages where code examples are shown.

ai.title: Remove security-page-restructure-plan.md
ai.summary: Deleted internal planning document `security-page-restructure-plan.md`. File contained roadmap for splitting security page into `/api-keys` and `/profile`. Purely internal artifact removal; no code or user-facing behavior changed.

eli5.text: The team deleted an internal planning note that described an idea for later splitting the security settings page into two separate pages: one for API keys and one for profile-related items like usage and sessions. Nothing on the website changed as a result. If you opened the website today, your security settings page would look exactly the same, because the plan described in the deleted note was never built.
